title: Proactive SLI decomposition and initiative taxonomy for quarterly reliability planning
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable taxonomy and operational flow that decomposes product-level SLIs into actionable sub-SLIs owned by platform, runtime, and surface teams, and use that decomposition to drive initiative prioritization and automated tranche triggers for error-budget rebalancing.

Why this work matters: As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private customers, outages and subtle regressions now have multi-team blast radius. Current SLO work is siloed (per-team SLIs) and makes quarterly planning opaque: teams either hoard error budget or overreact to short-lived blips. We need a playbook and a data model that ties user-facing SLOs to lower-level observables so PMs and Eng can confidently prioritize mitigations, schedule canaries, and automate rollback/mitigation when error budget burn crosses thresholds.

Deliverables:
- Initiative taxonomy doc that maps top-level SLIs (latency P95, availability, correctness rate) to 2–4 sub-SLIs per layer (networking, kernel scheduling, KV cache, batching) with suggested owners and measurement queries.
- Error-budget tranche policy template (soft warn / hard warn / gated mitigation) and recommended cadence for tranche resets and staircase rollouts.
- UI wireframes for an "Initiative Runner" panel in Console showing predicted burn curves, active tranches, and recommended actions (canary, throttle, fallback).
- Automation RFC for triggers (e.g., sustained 3x burn-rate over rolling 1h -> create incident + pause rollout) and for auto-scheduling cross-team war rooms.
- Pilot with two initiatives in Q2 (Batching tuning on Dedicated; KV cache TTL adjustments for hosted).

Scope (in-scope): SLI taxonomy, policies, Console UI mockups, automation RFC, pilot run and retrospective.
Scope (out-of-scope): Full implementation of automatic rollback in runtime (this will be a follow-on ENG project), billing changes, and cross-cloud routing policies beyond initial recommended knobs.

Success metrics:
- Time-to-decision on high-burn alerts reduced by 40% in pilot initiatives.
- 80% of platform incidents associated to pilot initiatives contain a mapped sub-SLI in taxonomy within two weeks.
- Pilot initiatives show measurable reduction in error-budget volatility (30% lower peak burn-rate) after applying recommended mitigations.

Stakeholders: Reliability PMs (Priya Raman), Runtime Eng (Marcus Liu), Console Product (Elena García), Observability (Samir Patel), Solutions/SE (Tess O'Connor).

Rollout plan: Research & taxonomy design (now) -> automation RFC and Console mocks (2 sprints) -> pilot implementation and monitoring (1 quarter) -> iterate and hand off operational playbooks to SREs.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Wrongly attributed sub-SLI causes churning between teams. Mitigation: require owner sign-off and run a 2-week validation window before any tranche-based enforcement.
- Risk: Noise in metrics leads to false alarms. Mitigation: rely on burn-rate windows and require sustained thresholds plus spike filters before action.

Notes on measurement: All sub-SLI queries should use the canonical telemetry sources (prod-traces, token-latency histogram, per-route errors) and attach a link to the query in the taxonomy doc. Use synthesized traffic for canary validation in pilot.
updates: 2025-11-05 — Priya Raman: Kickoff meeting with runtime and observability. Agreed on top-level SLIs: request latency P95, availability by route, structured-output correctness. Added initial list of candidate sub-SLIs for kernel scheduling and batching.

2025-11-18 — Marcus Liu: Ran exploratory queries to map latency spikes to batching window sizes. Found a consistent correlation between batch cutoff delays and P95 on short-seq requests. Added concrete query links: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency/batching-correlation

2025-12-02 — Elena García (Console PM): Reviewed initial wireframes. Recommended a compact "burn forecast" sparkline per initiative and a compact action menu (Pause rollout / Throttle / Run hunt). Created a follow-up ticket for mock accessibility checks.

2026-01-09 — Samir Patel (Observability): Implemented sub-SLI dashboards for the pilot initiatives and added cardinality limits to queries to avoid dashboard OOMs. Note: had to add a 5m aggregation window to reduce cardinality.

2026-02-20 — Cross-team review: Agreed on tranche policy thresholds (soft warn at 20% of tranche in 24h, hard warn 40%, automated mitigation at sustained 3x burn-rate for 1h). Decision: run pilot using soft/hard warn only for first month; defer automated mitigation until confidence tests pass.
2026-03-03 — Design review: Finalized Initiative Runner mock with show/hide for sub-SLIs and a recommended actions panel. Link to Figma: https://figma.redwood/initiative-runner/v1

2026-03-10 — Priya Raman: RFC draft for automation triggers posted for feedback. Next: schedule pilot kickoff with Solutions Eng and set SLAs for measurement validation (2 weeks) before tranche enforcement. Link: https://confluence.redwood/relhub/sli-decomposition-rfc
